C# by far, mostly because of .NET. It just makes everything so easy. CRUD programs, games, websites, doesn't matter, C# wins.

Only downside is going cross-platform. It's possible, and MS is starting to support it, but there's still a lot of annoyances to it. For now, I'd use C++ or Python if I wanted my stuff to run on Linux.

Really it depends on the task at hand, but in general I'm a fan of Java and Python. Perl is awesome for one-liners. Bash feels clunky, but I probably accomplish more actual work with it than anything else. I'm open to the possibility that the only reason C isn't my fav is because I don't know it well enough. Haskell and clojure and clisp are all fun to play with, but I'm yet to figure out how to actually do anything with them.

One thing is for sure: I'm not too crazy about fortran.

Python is my favorite scripting language, but it only beats perl by a pinch.

C for anything compiled, I'm looking at Rust a lot more lately, too.
Erlang because that's what I'm studying, and because it is hard. I feel like I'm in over my head at all times, but I know if I keep swimming I'll reach the shore.

C/C++, and I use them in conjunction these days since I do a lot of embedded work. C when necessary, C with classes when convenient, proper C++ when it's best.

There's a certain purity to it... I know a large handful of other languages, but C and C++ fill most of my use cases. Bash for quick tools, perl for somewhat more complex tools (especially when text processing is required), PHP+MySQL for websites, but C/C++ for the work that gets me paid.

F#. It's a functional language that can be fully OO if need be and can access/run full .Net.

I also quite like JavaScript's prototypal inheritance model as you can do some really abstract things in it that would require tons of statically typed code to pull off.

I actually like Java the best, because it's so strictly logical, even if that does result in a few weird quirks that you have to work around. I don't mind though because there's a clear reason the quirk is that way. (Switches not using Strings is a good example)
Scala tinkerer here. It makes for smaller code. I avoid SBT, Apache Commons and Eclipse.

Love python, miss curly brackets though; can be an eye sore depending on your text editor. Been working a lot in Java lately, it's nice but finlandia has the right idea in saying that most compiled things is best done in C.

Perl - You are quite sure it is installed on any Linux/Unix distro :-)

Bash - Same as Perl

Absolutely C#, and I say this as a formerly diehard C++ fanboy. C# just does exactly what you'd need it to and it does it better than anything else. It's compiled like C but also class-based like Java.

Lucid dreaming might be hard at first, it might even take a few years - - it did me - - but it was worth it. I don't dream anything I don't want to. I haven't had a nightmare in 5 years, since I began.

Realizing you're dreaming is the definition of lucid dreaming. You might not have any control at first, but that is how it is. It's gradual. The first step is realizing you're dreaming. The rest comes slowly and with effort.

There's no reason to become upset upon realizing you're dreaming. If it bothers you it's only because you think you have less control than you really do. If you are upset while dreaming, if you are lucid you can just wake up.
